pass_a_gloss: And let us not marvel if such great blessedness of the martyrs, which will be in deep peace and stillness of sea and good weather, must start from some condition reckoned more sullen and, so that I may name it thus, of the winter season. For before, journeying in winter on the narrow and pressed road, each of the blessed ones will need to display the steering which he acquired, in order that after these things there may happen the thing said in the Song of Songs to the bride who has swum through the winter: for my kinsman answers, it says, and says to me: stand up, come, the one near me, my beautiful one, my dove; because look, the winter went past, the rain went off, it journeyed for itself. And you, remember further that it is not possible in another way to hear 'the winter went past', unless you contest the present winter robustly and with good tension. And after the winter has gone past and the rain has gone off and journeyed for itself, the flowers will be seen; for those planted in the house of the Lord will bloom out in the courtyards of our God.
pass_b_english: Let us not be surprised if the blessedness of the martyrs, great as it is, which will be passed in deep peace, calm and fair weather, must begin from a state of things that is thought rather gloomy and, if I may call it so, wintry. For first each of the blessed, travelling the narrow and hard-pressed way (Matthew 7:14) in winter, will have to show the seamanship he has gained, so that afterwards there may come to pass what is said in the Song of Songs to the bride who has swum through the winter: “My beloved answers,” it says, “and says to me: Arise, come, my companion, my fair one, my dove; for see, the winter is past, the rain is gone, it has taken itself away” (Song of Solomon 2:10-11).

And you, keep this in mind as well: you cannot hear the words “The winter is past” unless you fight your way through the present winter with strength and vigour. And after the winter has passed and the rain has gone and taken itself away, the flowers will appear (Song of Solomon 2:12); for “those planted in the house of the Lord will blossom in the courts of our God” (Psalm 92:13).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 31); the old English was misaligned: it ran on into chapter 32 (the enemy who cannot persuade, idols as demons) and kept awkward literalisms ('swam through winter', 'no hearing ... unless the present winter be warred robustly'); this chapter is now translated alone and in full.
Taken as imperative ('And you, keep this in mind as well'), addressed to Origen's readers; the form can also be indicative ('you still remember'), which the old English used.

choices.issue: ἔστιν (Koetschau's correction of ἐστὴν MP Delarue)

choices.choice: 'seamanship' (steering a ship), keeping the sea image of winter storms, calm (γαλήνη) and fair weather.
